title: Cremorne Theatre
axis: +X along the approximate former street-front elevation; +Z roughly southwest outward through the reconstructed main entrance; +Y up from fixed approach.
source: Historical circa1934 original Cremorne Theatre only. Exact published archival file location[153.01873,-27.47262]retained as approximate site anchor, not a surveyed building centre; positional uncertainty about30m. No original footprint survives or is mapped. The30x18m hall and12/13x4m entrance annex outline is an explicit photo-ratio reconstruction, with concealed depth/dimensions and slightly gabled roof estimated. Current Cultural Centre Tunnel way530172035 retains original three coordinates solely as modern street context, never the old theatre footprint or a claim that current tunnel is the1934road. Visualization street-facing axis is perpendicular to this present contextual axis, roughly southwest; old street alignment and plaque/front facing are approximate by60degrees. The native archival caption places the theatre on the riverbank side of former Stanley Street between Peel and Melbourne. Archival point identity, approximate orientation and reconstructed extent are separately labelled. Modern gallery/campus excluded. Fixed approach[9,18]before independently sampled modern terrain/geometry;1934grade and host contact are not established.

geometryLabel: Historical1934 photo-estimated whole theatre and own entrance annex; no original mapped footprint

orientationControl.basis: Approximate street-facing visualization using archival site/caption and modern surrounding street axis; no1934bearing survey.

terrainContact.basis: Fixed reconstructed street-side approach before modern terrain and geometry. Historic ground/threshold and changed current grading unknown.

notes: Historical circa1934 original Cremorne Theatre on Stanley Street: complete theatre hall/tall louvred upper envelope and roof, lower street-front entrance annex/canopy, own scalloped/stepped entrance parapet and multi-light timber doors. Reconstruct a bounded exterior with honest hidden side/rear/roof estimates. The original burned in1954 and is not the modern QPAC namesake. Exclude surrounding street, adjoining businesses/structures, people, text lettering/posters and interior.
